en: Bro's notes on Atomic Habits, by James Clear. If you keep starting new habits on Monday and dropping them by Thursday, this one is for you. It answers a simple question: how do tiny, boring daily actions quietly add up to a completely different life?

Idea one. Tiny gains add up. The book argues that getting just one percent better each day looks like nothing at first. Think of reading two pages of your syllabus every night on the metro ride home. Tonight it feels useless. Keep it going for a year and you have covered hundreds of pages. Small choices compound in both directions, so your daily defaults matter more than rare heroic efforts. Try this today: Write down one small action you can repeat every single day this week.

Idea two. Systems beat goals. Everyone sitting in the exam hall has the same goal, to pass with good marks. So the goal alone cannot explain who succeeds. The author suggests you put your attention on the system, the daily process that produces the result. A goal is the score on the board. A system is how you practise at the nets every evening. Fix the process and results tend to follow. Try this today: Replace one big goal with a daily process you can actually follow.
